or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

Visualize the entropy of a code base with a 3d force-directed graph.

The more decoupled and modular a code base is, the more spread and clustered the graph will look like.

Ensure your code base decoupling by creating your own rules and enforcing them with dep-tree check

## Supported languages
## Install On Mac and Linux, it can be installed using brew: ```shell brew install dep-tree ``` Alternatively, on any platform including Windows it can be installed with `pip`... ```shell pip install python-dep-tree ``` ...or `npm`: ```shell npm install @dep-tree/cli ``` ## About Dep Tree `dep-tree` is a cli tool for visualizing the complexity of a code base, and creating rules for ensuring its loosely coupling. It works with files, meaning that each file is a node in the dependency tree: - It starts from one or more entrypoints, which are usually the main executable files in a program or the files that expose the contents of a library (like `package/main.py`, `src/index.ts`, `src/lib.rs`...). - It makes a parent node out of the root file, and one child node for each imported file. > [!NOTE] > it only takes into account local files, not files imported from external libraries. - That process is repeated recursively with all the imported files, until the file dependency graph is formed. - If rendering the **code base entropy**, the nodes will be rendered using a 3d force-directed graph in the browser. - If rendering the **dependency tree** in the terminal, the nodes will be placed in a human-readable way, and users can navigate through the graph using the keyboard. - If validating the **dependency rules** in a CI system, it will check that the dependencies between files match some boundaries declared in a `.dep-tree.yml` file. ## Usage ### Entropy Choose the file that will act as the root of the dependency graph (for example `src/index.ts`), and run: ```shell dep-tree entropy src/index.ts ``` You can also pass multiple files if you don't have a single entrypoint: ```shell dep-tree entropy src/* ``` It will open a browser window and will render your file dependency graph using a 3d force-directed graph. The spheres (files) will be placed mimicking some attraction/repulsion forces. Some parts of your code base will tend to gravitate together if they are tightly coupled, and will tend to be separated if they are loosely coupled. The 3d graph for a clean code base will have groups of nodes clustered together and clearly separated from other clusters:
The 3d graph for a tightly coupled code base will have all the nodes grouped together with no clustering and no clear separation between them:
### Explain Given two pieces of code, displays what are the dependencies between them. These pieces of code are specified using a glob patterns, for example: ```shell dep-tree explain 'src/products/**/*.go' 'src/orders/**/*.go' ``` > [!WARNING] > Make sure you wrap the two glob patterns with single quotes ('') or double quotes (""), > otherwise your shell might expand the globstars, and `dep-tree explain` will receive > an incorrect number of arguments. Map from glob pattern to list of glob patterns that define, using a "white list"
logic, what files can depend on what other files. For example:

```yml
check:
  allow:
    "src/products/**":
      - "src/products/**"
      - "src/common/**"
```

In the example above, any file under the `src/products` folder has the restriction of only
being able to import files that live either in the same `src/products` folder, or in the
`src/common` folder.

### `deny`:

Map from glob pattern to list of glob patterns that define, using a "black list"
logic, what dependencies are forbidden. For example:

```yml
check:
  deny:
    "api/routes.py":
      - "adapters/**"
```

In the example above, the file `api/routes.py` can import from anywhere but the `adapters` folder.

### `allowCircularDependencies`:

Boolean parameter that defines whether circular dependencies are allowed or not. By default
they are not allowed.

```yml
check:
  allowCircularDependencies: true
```

### `aliases`:

Map from string to glob pattern that gathers utility groups of glob patterns that
can be reused in the `deny` and `allow` fields. For example:

```yml
check:
  aliases:
    "common-stuff":
      - "src/common/**"
      - "src/utils/**"
      - "src/helpers/**"
  allow:
    "src/function.py":
      - "common-stuff"
      - "src/class.py"
```

is the same as saying:

```yml
check:
  allow:
    "src/function.py":
      - "src/common/**"
      - "src/utils/**"
      - "src/helpers/**"
      - "src/class.py"
```

### Example configuration file

A `schema.json` file is provided which can be used in IDEs for providing autocompletion on `.dep-tree.yml` files.

Dep Tree by default will read the configuration file in `.dep-tree.yml`, which is expected to be a file
that contains the following settings:

```yml
# Files that should be completely ignored by dep-tree. It's fine to ignore
# some big files that everyone depends on and that don't add
# value to the visualization, like auto generated code.
exclude:
  - 'some-glob-pattern/**/*.ts'

# The only files that will be included by dep-tree. If a file does not
# match any of the provided patterns, it is ignored.
only:
  - 'some-glob-pattern/**/*.ts'

# Whether to unwrap re-exports to the target file or not.
# Imagine that you have the following setup:
#
#  src/index.ts     -> import { foo } from './foo'
#  src/foo/index.ts -> export { bar as foo } from './bar'
#  src/foo/bar.ts   -> export function bar() {}
#
# If `unwrapExports` is true, a dependency will be created from
# `src/index.ts` to `src/foo/bar.ts`, and the middle file `src/foo/index.ts`
# will be ignored, as it's just there for re-exporting the `bar` symbol,
# which is actually declared on `src/foo/bar.ts`
#
# If `unwrapExports` is false, re-exported symbols will not be traced back
# to where they are declared, and instead two dependencies will be created:
# - from `src/index.ts` to `src/foo/index.ts`
# - from `src/foo/index.ts` to `src/foo/bar.ts`
#
# Entropy visualization tends to lead to better results if this is set to `false`,
# but CLI rendering is slightly better with this set to `true`.
unwrapExports: false

# Check configuration for the `dep-tree check` command. Dep Tree will check for dependency
# violation rules declared here, and fail if there is at least one unsatisfied rule.
check:

  # these files as root nodes. Typically, an application has only one entrypoint, which
  # is the executable file (`src/index.ts`, `main.py`, `src/lib.rs`, ...), but here
  # you can declare as many as you want.
  entrypoints:
    - src/index.ts

  # Whether to allow circular dependencies or not. Languages typically allow
  # having circular dependencies, but that has an impact in execution path
  # traceability, so you might want to disallow it.
  allowCircularDependencies: false

  # dependencies that a file matching a key glob pattern might have. If file that
  # matches a key glob pattern depends on another file that does not match any of
  # the glob patterns declared in the values array, the check will fail.
  allow:
    # example: any file in `src/products` can only depend on files that are also
    # in the `src/products` folder or in the `src/helpers` folder.
    'src/products/**':
      - 'src/products/**'
      - 'src/helpers/**'
    # additionally, instead of providing a simple list of allowed dependencies, you
    # can also provide the reason for this restriction to exist, that way, when if the
    # check fails, an informative error is displayed through stderr.
    'src/users/**':
      to:
        - 'src/helpers/**'
      reason: The Users domain is only allowed to import helper code, nothing else

  # dependencies. If a file that matches a key glob pattern depends on another
  # file that matches at least one of the glob patterns declared in the values
  # array, the check will fail.
  deny:
    # example: files inside `src/products` cannot depend on files inside `src/users`,
    # as they are supposed to belong to different domains.
    'src/products/**':
      - 'src/users/**'
    # additionally, instead of providing a simple list of forbidden dependencies, you
    # can also provide the reason for each individual restriction to exist. If one of
    # these rules is broken, the reason will be displayed through stderr
    'src/users/**':
      - to: 'src/products/**'

      - to: 'src/orders/**'

  # on, because they are supposed to be common helpers, or parts that are actually
```

## Motivation

As codebases expand and teams grow, complexity inevitably creeps in.
While maintaining a cohesive and organized structure is key to
a project's scalability and maintainability,
the current developer toolbox often falls short in one critical
area: file structure and dependency management.

Luckily, the community has come up with very useful tools
for keeping our projects in check:

- **Type checkers** ensure correct interactions between code segments.
- **Linters** elevate code quality and maintain a consistent style.
- **Formatters** guarantee a uniform code format throughout.
- But what about file structure and file dependency management...

Dep Tree is a dedicated tool addressing this very challenge,
it aids developers in preserving a project's structural integrity
throughout its lifecycle. And with integration capabilities in CI systems,
the tool ensures that this architectural "harmony" remains undisturbed.

## Supported languages

Visualize the entropy of a code base with a 3d force-directed graph.

The more decoupled and modular a code base is, the more spread and clustered the graph will look like.

## Install On Mac and Linux, it can be installed using brew: ```shell brew install dep-tree ``` Alternatively, on any platform including Windows it can be installed with `pip`... ```shell pip install python-dep-tree ``` ...or `npm`: ```shell npm install @dep-tree/cli ``` ## About Dep Tree `dep-tree` is a cli tool for visualizing the complexity of a code base, and creating rules for ensuring its loosely coupling. It works with files, meaning that each file is a node in the dependency tree: - It starts from one or more entrypoints, which are usually the main executable files in a program or the files that expose the contents of a library (like `package/main.py`, `src/index.ts`, `src/lib.rs`...). - It makes a parent node out of the root file, and one child node for each imported file. > [!NOTE] > it only takes into account local files, not files imported from external libraries. - That process is repeated recursively with all the imported files, until the file dependency graph is formed. - If rendering the **code base entropy**, the nodes will be rendered using a 3d force-directed graph in the browser. - If rendering the **dependency tree** in the terminal, the nodes will be placed in a human-readable way, and users can navigate through the graph using the keyboard. - If validating the **dependency rules** in a CI system, it will check that the dependencies between files match some boundaries declared in a `.dep-tree.yml` file. ## Usage ### Entropy Choose the file that will act as the root of the dependency graph (for example `src/index.ts`), and run: ```shell dep-tree entropy src/index.ts ``` You can also pass multiple files if you don't have a single entrypoint: ```shell dep-tree entropy src/* ``` It will open a browser window and will render your file dependency graph using a 3d force-directed graph. The spheres (files) will be placed mimicking some attraction/repulsion forces. Some parts of your code base will tend to gravitate together if they are tightly coupled, and will tend to be separated if they are loosely coupled. The 3d graph for a clean code base will have groups of nodes clustered together and clearly separated from other clusters:
The 3d graph for a tightly coupled code base will have all the nodes grouped together with no clustering and no clear separation between them:

These pieces of code are specified using a glob patterns, for example: ```shell dep-tree explain 'src/products/**/*.go' 'src/orders/**/*.go' ``` > [!WARNING] > Make sure you wrap the two glob patterns with single quotes ('') or double quotes (""), > otherwise your shell might expand the globstars, and `dep-tree explain` will receive > an incorrect number of arguments. This flag is useful for retrieving any external dependencies of a specific folder: ```shell # Retrieves dependencies from files in src/products to any other file that is not inside src/products dep-tree explain 'src/products/**/*.go' '**/*.go' --overlap-left ``` - `--overlap-right`: when the left and right glob patterns have some files in common, keep only the common files at the right, and discard them from the left. def parse_scalar(s):
    s = s.strip()
    if s == "":
        return ""
    if s.lower() == "true":
        return True
    if s.lower() == "false":
        return False
    if s.lower() in ("null", "~"):
        return None
    # strip quotes
    if len(s) >= 2 and ((s[0] == "'" and s[-1] == "'") or (s[0] == '"' and s[-1] == '"')):
        return s[1:-1]
    # try int
    try:
        if s.isdigit() or (s.lstrip('-').isdigit()):
            return int(s)
    except:
        pass
    return s

def parse_yaml_content(text):
    # simple yaml parser for subset
    lines = text.splitlines()
    enriched = []
    for line in lines:
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(' '))
        enriched.append((indent, stripped, line))
    root = {}
    stack = [(-1, root)]
    i = 0
    while i < len(enriched):
        indent, stripped, raw = enriched[i]
        # pop to parent
        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        if not stack:
            stack = [(-1, root)]
        parent_indent, parent = stack[-1]
        if stripped.startswith('- '):
            if not isinstance(parent, list):
                # error case: parent should be list, but we may have created dict incorrectly
                # Try to find nearest list in stack
                # Look backwards for list
                found = None
                for idx in range(len(stack)-1, -1, -1):
                    if isinstance(stack[idx][1], list):
                        found = stack[idx][1]
                        # pop until that
                        while stack[-1][1] is not found:
                            stack.pop()
                        parent = found
                        break
                if not isinstance(parent, list):
                    # fallback: treat as error
                    i+=1
                    continue
            value_str = stripped[2:].strip()
            if not value_str:
                new_dict = {}
                parent.append(new_dict)
                stack.append((indent, new_dict))
            elif ':' in value_str:
                # dict inside list
                # handle "- key: value" possibly with more
                # split first colon
                # but value_str may be "to: 'src/products/**'"
                # we need to create dict with that key
                k, v = value_str.split(':', 1)
                k = k.strip().strip('\'"')
                v = v.strip()
                new_dict = {}
                if v:
                    new_dict[k] = parse_scalar(v)
                else:
                    # value empty, look ahead for list/dict
                    if i+1 < len(enriched) and enriched[i+1][0] > indent:
                        nxt_indent, nxt_stripped, _ = enriched[i+1]
                        if nxt_stripped.startswith('- '):
                            new_dict[k] = []
                            # push dict then list? We'll push dict first, then list for future items
                            # But the list items for this key are at higher indent than current "-"
                            # They should be children of new_dict[k] list
                            parent.append(new_dict)
                            stack.append((indent, new_dict))
                            # also push the list container
                            stack.append((indent+2, new_dict[k]))
                            i+=1
                            continue
                        else:
                            new_dict[k] = {}
                            parent.append(new_dict)
                            stack.append((indent, new_dict))
                            stack.append((indent+2, new_dict[k]))
                            i+=1
                            continue
                parent.append(new_dict)
                stack.append((indent, new_dict))
            else:
                parent.append(parse_scalar(value_str))
        elif ':' in stripped:
            # dict entry
            # split first colon
            k, v = stripped.split(':', 1)
            k = k.strip().strip('\'"')
            v = v.strip()
            if not isinstance(parent, dict):
                # parent is list's dict? But we are inside list item dict, parent is dict
                # Need to find nearest dict
                found = None
                for idx in range(len(stack)-1, -1, -1):
                    if isinstance(stack[idx][1], dict):
                        found = stack[idx][1]
                        break
                if found is not None:
                    parent = found
                else:
                    i+=1
                    continue
            if not v:
                # look ahead
                if i+1 < len(enriched) and enriched[i+1][0] > indent:
                    nxt_indent, nxt_stripped, _ = enriched[i+1]
                    if nxt_stripped.startswith('- '):
                        new_list = []
                        parent[k] = new_list
                        stack.append((indent, new_list))
                    else:
                        new_dict = {}
                        parent[k] = new_dict
                        stack.append((indent, new_dict))
                else:
                    parent[k] = None
            else:
                parent[k] = parse_scalar(v)
        else:
            # bare value? ignore
            pass
        i+=1
    return root

def load_config(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "missing"
    try:
        content = open(path, 'r').read()
        # try yaml library if available
        try:
            import yaml
            data = yaml.safe_load(content)
            if data is None:
                data = {}
            return data, None
        except ImportError:
            # use our parser
            # quick check for invalid yaml like "invalid: ["
            # We'll try to parse and if fails, return error
            # Detect obvious invalid: line with "invalid: [" and no closing
            if "invalid:" in content and "[" in content and "]" not in content.split("invalid:")[1].split("\n")[0]:
                raise Exception("yaml: line 1: did not find expected node content")
            data = parse_yaml_content(content)
            return data, None
        except Exception as e:
            # yaml parse error
            # produce generic message
            msg = str(e)
            # original message is "yaml: line 1: did not find expected node content"
            # We'll use that if msg contains that
            if "did not find expected node content" in msg or "expected node content" in msg:
                return None, "yaml: line 1: did not find expected node content"
            else:
                return None, msg
    except Exception as e:
        return None, str(e)

def fnv1a(s):
    h = 2166136261
    for b in s.encode():
        h ^= b
        h = (h * 16777619) & 0xffffffff
    return h

def glob_match(path, pattern):
    # use pathlib PurePosixPath match
    # pattern may contain single quotes
    # Use fnmatch with pathlib
    try:
        return pathlib.PurePosixPath(path).match(pattern)
    except:
        # fallback to fnmatch
        return fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern)

def should_include(rel_path, exclude_patterns, only_patterns):
    # exclude
    for pat in exclude_patterns:
        if glob_match(rel_path, pat):
            return False
    if only_patterns:
        for pat in only_patterns:
            if glob_match(rel_path, pat):
                return True
        return False
    return True

def expand_glob(pattern):
    # returns list of files matching pattern, relative to cwd
    # If pattern contains * or ? or [, use glob
    # else check existence
    if any(c in pattern for c in "*?["):
        matched = glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)
        # filter only files
        files = [f for f in matched if os.path.isfile(f)]
        # also need to handle that glob may return with ./ prefix? Keep as is but normalize
        # Normalize to posix and remove leading ./
        normed = []
        for f in files:
            # glob returns as pattern is given; we want relative posix path
            # Use os.path.relpath? But glob already relative to cwd if pattern relative
            # Just normalize
            nf = os.path.normpath(f)
            # Convert to posix with /
            nf = nf.replace(os.sep, "/")
            normed.append(nf)
        return sorted(normed)
    else:
        # literal path
        if os.path.isfile(pattern):
            return [os.path.normpath(pattern).replace(os.sep, "/")]
        # also check if pattern without extension but file exists with extension? No
        return []

def find_all_files(exclude_patterns, only_patterns, extensions=None):
    # scan all files under cwd recursively
    # extensions: list like [".js",".py"] or None for all
    all_files = []
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(".", topdown=True):
        # skip hidden dirs like .git, node_modules? But we should include scanning but respect exclude
        # Modify dirs in-place to skip large dirs?
        # Keep scanning
        for fname in files:
            fpath = os.path.join(root, fname)
            # normalize
            rel = os.path.normpath(fpath).replace(os.sep, "/")
            if rel.startswith("./"):
                rel = rel[2:]
            if extensions:
                ext = os.path.splitext(fname)[1]
                if ext not in extensions:
                    continue
            if should_include(rel, exclude_patterns, only_patterns):
                all_files.append(rel)
    return all_files

def resolve_js_import(current_file, import_path, project_root):
    # current_file is relative path like "src/main.js" or "a.js"
    # import_path is string like "./foo", "../bar", "@/util"
    # project_root is cwd (for relative)
    # returns relative path of target file if found, else None
    if import_path.startswith("."):
        base_dir = os.path.dirname(current_file)
        # handle "./foo" vs "../foo"
        target = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base_dir, import_path)).replace(os.sep, "/")
        # try candidates
        candidates = []
        # if target has extension, try directly
        if os.path.splitext(target)[1] in (".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".mjs",".cjs",".json"):
            candidates.append(target)
        else:
            for ext in [".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".mjs",".cjs",".js",".ts"]:
                candidates.append(target + ext)
            # index files
            for ext in [".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx"]:
                candidates.append(os.path.join(target, "index"+ext).replace(os.sep,"/"))
        for cand in candidates:
            # cand is relative to cwd
            # check existence relative to project_root? project_root is cwd
            abs_path = os.path.join(project_root, cand) if not os.path.isabs(cand) else cand
            # also need to handle that target may be like "./foo" without leading ./? Already normalized
            if os.path.isfile(cand) or os.path.isfile(abs_path):
                # return relative path normalized
                # Prefer relative from project_root (cwd)
                rel = os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
                if rel.startswith("./"):
                    rel = rel[2:]
                return rel
        return None
    elif import_path.startswith("/"):
        return None
    else:
        # non-relative, could be alias or package name
        # For alias "@/util", strip "@/" and try to find file
        if import_path.startswith("@/"):
            stripped = import_path[2:]
            # try project_root + stripped
            # stripped may be "util" or "util.js"
            candidates = []
            # try with extensions
            if os.path.splitext(stripped)[1]:
                candidates.append(stripped)
            else:
                for ext in [".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".mjs",".cjs"]:
                    candidates.append(stripped + ext)
                for ext in [".js",".ts"]:
                    candidates.append(os.path.join(stripped, "index"+ext).replace(os.sep,"/"))
                # also try src/stripped ?
                for ext in [".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx"]:
                    candidates.append(os.path.join("src", stripped + ext).replace(os.sep,"/"))
                    candidates.append(os.path.join("src", stripped, "index"+ext).replace(os.sep,"/"))
            for cand in candidates:
                if os.path.isfile(cand):
                    return os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
            return None
        else:
            # check for workspace: if js-workspaces true, try to find package
            # Simplify: treat as external
            return None

def parse_js_file(filepath):
    # returns deps, errors
    try:
        content = open(filepath, 'r', errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    deps = []
    errors = []
    # regex for imports
    # import ... from 'path' or import 'path'
    patterns = [
        r'import\s+(?:[^\'"]*?\s+from\s+)?[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]',
        r'export\s+(?:[^\'"]*?\s+from\s+)?[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]',
        r'require\s*\(\s*[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]\s*\)',
        r'import\s*\(\s*[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]\s*\)',  # dynamic import
    ]
    imports = []
    for pat in patterns:
        for m in re.finditer(pat, content):
            imports.append(m.group(1))
    for imp in imports:
        # only consider relative or alias
        if imp.startswith(".") or imp.startswith("@/"):
            resolved = resolve_js_import(filepath, imp, os.getcwd())
            if resolved:
                deps.append(resolved)
            else:
                # if relative import and not found, it's an error
                if imp.startswith("."):
                    errors.append(f"could not perform relative import for '{imp}' because the file or dir was not found")
        else:
            # check if it's a workspace package? ignore
            pass
    return deps, errors

def parse_python_file(filepath, exclude_conditional=False):
    try:
        content = open(filepath, 'r', errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []

    except:

    deps = []

    project_root = os.getcwd()
    # collect imports
    # Walk with conditional tracking

        # If is_cond, then children are conditional

        for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
            if isinstance(child, ast.Import):
                if exclude_conditional and new_cond and isinstance(node, (ast.If, ast.Try)):
                    continue

                # The flag says exclude imports wrapped inside if or try statements.
                # So if we are inside If/Try, skip.
                if exclude_conditional and in_conditional:
                    # need to know if import is directly inside conditional
                    # We propagate in_conditional correctly
                    pass
                # For now, handle: if exclude_conditional and in_conditional (meaning ancestor is If/Try), skip
                if exclude_conditional and in_conditional:
                    continue

    cycles = []

        for w in graph.get(v, []):

def fnv1a(s):
    h = 2166136261
    for b in s.encode():
        h ^= b
        h = (h * 16777619) & 0xffffffff
    return h

def glob_match(path, pattern):
    try:
        return pathlib.PurePosixPath(path).match(pattern)
    except:
        return fnmatch.fnmatch(path, pattern)

def should_include(rel_path, exclude_patterns, only_patterns):
    for pat in exclude_patterns:
        if glob_match(rel_path, pat):
            return False
    if only_patterns:
        for pat in only_patterns:
            if glob_match(rel_path, pat):
                return True
        return False
    return True

def expand_glob(pattern):
    if any(c in pattern for c in "*?["):
        matched = glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True)
        files = [f for f in matched if os.path.isfile(f)]
        normed = []
        for f in files:
            nf = os.path.normpath(f).replace(os.sep, "/")
            if nf.startswith("./"):
                nf = nf[2:]
            normed.append(nf)
        return sorted(normed)
    else:
        if os.path.isfile(pattern):
            nf = os.path.normpath(pattern).replace(os.sep, "/")
            if nf.startswith("./"):
                nf = nf[2:]
            return [nf]
        return []

def parse_scalar(s):
    s=s.strip()
    if s=="": return ""
    if s.lower()=="true": return True
    if s.lower()=="false": return False
    if s.lower() in ("null","~"): return None
    if len(s)>=2 and ((s[0]=="'" and s[-1]=="'") or (s[0]=='"' and s[-1]=='"')):
        return s[1:-1]
    try:
        if s.lstrip('-').isdigit():
            return int(s)
    except:
        pass
    return s

def parse_yaml_simple(text):
    lines=text.splitlines()
    enriched=[]
    for line in lines:
        stripped=line.strip()
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
            continue
        indent=len(line)-len(line.lstrip(' '))
        enriched.append((indent, stripped, line))
    root={}
    stack=[(-1, root)]
    i=0
    while i < len(enriched):
        indent, stripped, raw = enriched[i]
        while stack and stack[-1][0] >= indent:
            stack.pop()
        if not stack:
            stack=[(-1, root)]
        parent = stack[-1][1]
        if stripped.startswith('- '):
            if not isinstance(parent, list):
                # find nearest list
                found=None
                for idx in range(len(stack)-1,-1,-1):
                    if isinstance(stack[idx][1], list):
                        found=stack[idx][1]
                        while stack[-1][1] is not found:
                            stack.pop()
                        parent=found
                        break
                if not isinstance(parent, list):
                    i+=1
                    continue
            value_str=stripped[2:].strip()
            if not value_str:
                new_dict={}
                parent.append(new_dict)
                stack.append((indent, new_dict))
            elif ':' in value_str:
                k,v = value_str.split(':',1)
                k=k.strip().strip('\'"')
                v=v.strip()
                new_dict={}
                if v:
                    new_dict[k]=parse_scalar(v)
                else:
                    if i+1 < len(enriched) and enriched[i+1][0] > indent:
                        nxt_indent, nxt_stripped, _ = enriched[i+1]
                        if nxt_stripped.startswith('- '):
                            new_dict[k]=[]
                            parent.append(new_dict)
                            stack.append((indent, new_dict))
                            stack.append((indent+2, new_dict[k]))
                            i+=1
                            continue
                        else:
                            new_dict[k]={}
                            parent.append(new_dict)
                            stack.append((indent, new_dict))
                            stack.append((indent+2, new_dict[k]))
                            i+=1
                            continue
                parent.append(new_dict)
                stack.append((indent, new_dict))
            else:
                parent.append(parse_scalar(value_str))
        elif ':' in stripped:
            k,v = stripped.split(':',1)
            k=k.strip().strip('\'"')
            v=v.strip()
            if not isinstance(parent, dict):
                found=None
                for idx in range(len(stack)-1,-1,-1):
                    if isinstance(stack[idx][1], dict):
                        found=stack[idx][1]
                        break
                if found is not None:
                    parent=found
                else:
                    i+=1
                    continue
            if not v:
                if i+1 < len(enriched) and enriched[i+1][0] > indent:
                    nxt_indent, nxt_stripped, _ = enriched[i+1]
                    if nxt_stripped.startswith('- '):
                        new_list=[]
                        parent[k]=new_list
                        stack.append((indent, new_list))
                    else:
                        new_dict={}
                        parent[k]=new_dict
                        stack.append((indent, new_dict))
                else:
                    parent[k]=None
            else:
                parent[k]=parse_scalar(v)
        i+=1
    return root

def load_config(path):
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, "missing"
    try:
        content=open(path,'r').read()
        # quick invalid check
        if "invalid:" in content:
            # simulate yaml error if invalid: [
            for line in content.splitlines():
                if "invalid:" in line and "[" in line and "]" not in line.split("invalid:")[1]:
                    raise Exception("yaml: line 1: did not find expected node content")
        try:
            import yaml
            data=yaml.safe_load(content)
            if data is None:
                data={}
            return data, None
        except ImportError:
            data=parse_yaml_simple(content)
            return data, None
        except Exception as e:
            msg=str(e)
            if "did not find expected node content" in msg or "expected node content" in msg:
                return None, "yaml: line 1: did not find expected node content"
            else:
                return None, msg
    except Exception as e:
        return None, str(e)

def get_exclude_only(config_data, cli_exclude, cli_only):
    cfg_exclude=[]
    cfg_only=[]
    if isinstance(config_data, dict):
        if "exclude" in config_data:
            v=config_data["exclude"]
            if isinstance(v, list):
                cfg_exclude=[str(x).strip().strip('\'"') for x in v]
            elif isinstance(v, str):
                cfg_exclude=[v]
        if "only" in config_data:
            v=config_data["only"]
            if isinstance(v, list):
                cfg_only=[str(x).strip().strip('\'"') for x in v]
            elif isinstance(v, str):
                cfg_only=[v]
    return cfg_exclude+cli_exclude, cfg_only+cli_only

def resolve_js_import(current_file, import_path):
    if import_path.startswith("."):
        base_dir=os.path.dirname(current_file)
        target=os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base_dir, import_path)).replace(os.sep, "/")
        candidates=[]
        if os.path.splitext(target)[1] in (".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".mjs",".cjs",".json"):
            candidates.append(target)
        else:
            for ext in [".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".mjs",".cjs"]:
                candidates.append(target+ext)
            for ext in [".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx"]:
                candidates.append(os.path.join(target, "index"+ext).replace(os.sep,"/"))
        for cand in candidates:
            nf=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
            if nf.startswith("./"):
                nf=nf[2:]
            if os.path.isfile(nf) or os.path.isfile(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), nf)):
                return nf
        return None
    elif import_path.startswith("@/"):
        stripped=import_path[2:]
        candidates=[]
        if os.path.splitext(stripped)[1]:
            candidates.append(stripped)
        else:
            for ext in [".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".mjs",".cjs"]:
                candidates.append(stripped+ext)
            for ext in [".js",".ts"]:
                candidates.append(os.path.join(stripped, "index"+ext).replace(os.sep,"/"))
            for ext in [".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx"]:
                candidates.append(os.path.join("src", stripped+ext).replace(os.sep,"/"))
                candidates.append(os.path.join("src", stripped, "index"+ext).replace(os.sep,"/"))
        for cand in candidates:
            nf=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
            if nf.startswith("./"):
                nf=nf[2:]
            if os.path.isfile(nf):
                return nf
        return None
    else:
        return None

def parse_js_file(filepath):
    try:
        content=open(filepath,'r',errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    deps=[]
    errors=[]
    patterns=[r'import\s+(?:[^\'"]*?\s+from\s+)?[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]', r'export\s+(?:[^\'"]*?\s+from\s+)?[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]', r'require\s*\(\s*[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]\s*\)', r'import\s*\(\s*[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]\s*\)']
    imports=[]
    for pat in patterns:
        for m in re.finditer(pat, content):
            imports.append(m.group(1))
    for imp in imports:
        if imp.startswith(".") or imp.startswith("@/"):
            resolved=resolve_js_import(filepath, imp)
            if resolved:
                deps.append(resolved)
            else:
                if imp.startswith("."):
                    errors.append(f"could not perform relative import for '{imp}' because the file or dir was not found")
    return deps, errors

def parse_python_file(filepath, exclude_conditional=False):
    try:
        content=open(filepath,'r',errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    try:
        tree=ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
    except:
        return [], []
    deps=[]
    project_root=os.getcwd()
    def walk(node, cond=False):
        cur_cond=cond or isinstance(node, (ast.If, ast.Try))
        for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
            if isinstance(child, ast.Import):
                if exclude_conditional and cur_cond:
                    continue
                for alias in child.names:
                    res=resolve_py_import(filepath, alias.name, 0, project_root)
                    if res:
                        deps.append(res)
            elif isinstance(child, ast.ImportFrom):
                if exclude_conditional and cur_cond:
                    continue
                mod=child.module if child.module else ""
                level=child.level
                res=resolve_py_import(filepath, mod, level, project_root, child.names)
                if res:
                    if isinstance(res, list):
                        deps.extend(res)
                    else:
                        deps.append(res)
            else:
                walk(child, cur_cond)
    walk(tree, False)
    return sorted(set(deps)), []

def resolve_py_import(current_file, mod, level, project_root, names=None):
    if level is None:
        level=0
    if level==0:
        if not mod:
            return None
        base=mod.replace('.','/')
        candidates=[base+".py", os.path.join(base,"__init__.py")]
        for cand in candidates:
            rel=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
            if rel.startswith("./"):
                rel=rel[2:]
            if os.path.isfile(cand) or os.path.isfile(os.path.join(project_root, cand)):
                return rel
            alt=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(current_file), cand)
            altr=os.path.normpath(alt).replace(os.sep,"/")
            if altr.startswith("./"):
                altr=altr[2:]
            if os.path.isfile(alt):
                return altr
        return None
    else:
        base_dir=os.path.dirname(current_file)
        for _ in range(level-1):
            base_dir=os.path.dirname(base_dir)
        if mod:
            base=mod.replace('.','/')
            candidates=[os.path.join(base_dir, base+".py"), os.path.join(base_dir, base, "__init__.py")]
            for cand in candidates:
                if os.path.isfile(cand):
                    rel=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
                    if rel.startswith("./"):
                        rel=rel[2:]
                    return rel
            return None
        else:
            results=[]
            if names:
                for alias in names:
                    mod_name=alias.name
                    candidates=[os.path.join(base_dir, mod_name+".py"), os.path.join(base_dir, mod_name, "__init__.py")]
                    for cand in candidates:
                        if os.path.isfile(cand):
                            rel=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
                            if rel.startswith("./"):
                                rel=rel[2:]
                            results.append(rel)
                            break
            if results:
                return results
            return None

def parse_go_file(filepath):
    try:
        content=open(filepath,'r',errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    deps=[]
    errors=[]
    # find go.mod
    mod_name=None
    go_root=None
    cur=os.path.abspath(os.getcwd())
    while True:
        gm=os.path.join(cur, "go.mod")
        if os.path.isfile(gm):
            try:
                for line in open(gm).read().splitlines():
                    line=line.strip()
                    if line.startswith("module "):
                        mod_name=line.split()[1]
                        go_root=cur
                        break
            except:
                pass
            break
        parent=os.path.dirname(cur)
        if parent==cur:
            break
        cur=parent
    if not mod_name:
        return [], []
    imports=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'import\s*\(\s*([^)]*?)\s*\)', content, re.DOTALL):
        block=m.group(1)
        for q in re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', block):
            imports.append(q)
    for m in re.finditer(r'import\s+"([^"]+)"', content):
        imports.append(m.group(1))
    # dedupe
    imports=list(set(imports))
    for imp in imports:
        if mod_name and imp.startswith(mod_name):
            suffix=imp[len(mod_name):].lstrip("/")
            target_dir=os.path.join(go_root, suffix) if suffix else go_root
            if os.path.isdir(target_dir):
                for fname in os.listdir(target_dir):
                    if fname.endswith(".go"):
                        abs_file=os.path.join(target_dir, fname)
                        try:
                            rel=os.path.relpath(abs_file, os.getcwd()).replace(os.sep,"/")
                        except:
                            rel=os.path.join(suffix, fname).replace(os.sep,"/")
                        deps.append(rel)
            else:
                if os.path.isfile(target_dir+".go"):
                    rel=os.path.relpath(target_dir+".go", os.getcwd()).replace(os.sep,"/")
                    deps.append(rel)
                else:
                    errors.append(f"open {target_dir}: no such file or directory")
    return sorted(set(deps)), errors

def parse_rust_file(filepath):
    try:
        content=open(filepath,'r',errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    deps=[]
    errors=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'^\s*(?:pub\s+)?mod\s+(\w+)\s*;', content, re.MULTILINE):
        mod=m.group(1)
        base_dir=os.path.dirname(filepath)
        candidates=[os.path.join(base_dir, mod+".rs"), os.path.join(base_dir, mod, "mod.rs"), os.path.join("src", mod+".rs"), os.path.join("src", mod, "mod.rs")]
        found=None
        for cand in candidates:
            if os.path.isfile(cand):
                found=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
                if found.startswith("./"):
                    found=found[2:]
                break
        if found:
            deps.append(found)
        else:
            abs_dir=os.path.abspath(base_dir) if base_dir else os.path.abspath(".")
            errors.append(f"could not find mod {mod} while looking in dir {abs_dir}")
    return deps, errors

def parse_file(filepath, exclude_conditional=False):
    ext=os.path.splitext(filepath)[1]
    if ext==".py":
        return parse_python_file(filepath, exclude_conditional)
    elif ext in (".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".mjs",".cjs"):
        return parse_js_file(filepath)
    elif ext==".go":
        return parse_go_file(filepath)
    elif ext==".rs":
        return parse_rust_file(filepath)
    else:
        return [], []

def build_graph(entry_files, exclude_patterns, only_patterns, python_exclude=False):
    graph={}
    errors={}
    visited=set()
    queue=entry_files[:]
    idx=0
    while idx < len(queue):
        f=queue[idx]
        idx+=1
        if f in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(f)
        if not os.path.isfile(f):
            continue
        deps, errs = parse_file(f, python_exclude)
        filtered=[]
        for d in deps:
            if not should_include(d, exclude_patterns, only_patterns):
                continue
            filtered.append(d)
            if d not in visited and d not in queue:
                queue.append(d)
        filtered=sorted(set(filtered))
        graph[f]=filtered
        if errs:
            errors[f]=errs
    return graph, errors, visited

def build_tree_structure(entry, graph):
    tree={}
    circular=[]
    def dfs(node, path):
        if node in path:
            idx=path.index(node)
            cycle=path[idx:]+[node]
            if cycle not in circular:
                circular.append(cycle)
            return None
        path.append(node)
        deps=graph.get(node, [])
        if not deps:
            path.pop()
            return None
        subtree={}
        for dep in deps:
            if dep in path:
                idx=path.index(dep)
                cycle=path[idx:]+[dep]
                if cycle not in circular:
                    circular.append(cycle)
                subtree[dep]=None
            else:
                child=dfs(dep, path)
                subtree[dep]=child
        path.pop()
        return subtree if subtree else None
    result=dfs(entry, [])
    if result is None:
        tree={entry: None}
    else:
        tree={entry: result}
    return tree, circular

def detect_all_cycles(graph):
    cycles=[]
    visited=set()
    stack=[]
    on_stack=set()
    def dfs(v):
        visited.add(v)
        stack.append(v)
        on_stack.add(v)
        for w in graph.get(v, []):
            if w not in visited:
                dfs(w)
            elif w in on_stack:
                idx=stack.index(w)
                cycle=stack[idx:]+[w]
                if cycle not in cycles:
                    cycles.append(cycle)
        stack.pop()
        on_stack.remove(v)
    for node in list(graph.keys()):
        if node not in visited:
            dfs(node)
    return cycles

def parse_js_file(filepath):
    try:
        content=open(filepath,'r',errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    deps=[]
    errors=[]
    patterns=[r'import\s+(?:[^\'"]*?\s+from\s+)?[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]', r'export\s+(?:[^\'"]*?\s+from\s+)?[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]', r'require\s*\(\s*[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]\s*\)', r'import\s*\(\s*[\'"]([^\'"]+)[\'"]\s*\)']
    imports=[]
    for pat in patterns:
        for m in re.finditer(pat, content):
            imports.append(m.group(1))
    for imp in imports:
        if imp.startswith(".") or imp.startswith("@/"):
            resolved=resolve_js_import(filepath, imp)
            if resolved:
                deps.append(resolved)
            else:
                if imp.startswith("."):
                    errors.append(f"could not perform relative import for '{imp}' because the file or dir was not found")
    return deps, errors

def parse_python_file(filepath, exclude_conditional=False):
    try:
        content=open(filepath,'r',errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    try:
        tree=ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
    except:
        return [], []
    deps=[]
    project_root=os.getcwd()
    def walk(node, cond=False):
        cur_cond=cond or isinstance(node, (ast.If, ast.Try))
        for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
            if isinstance(child, ast.Import):
                if exclude_conditional and cur_cond:
                    continue
                for alias in child.names:
                    res=resolve_py_import(filepath, alias.name, 0, project_root)
                    if res:
                        deps.append(res)
            elif isinstance(child, ast.ImportFrom):
                if exclude_conditional and cur_cond:
                    continue
                mod=child.module if child.module else ""
                level=child.level
                res=resolve_py_import(filepath, mod, level, project_root, child.names)
                if res:
                    if isinstance(res, list):
                        deps.extend(res)
                    else:
                        deps.append(res)
            else:
                walk(child, cur_cond)
    walk(tree, False)
    return sorted(set(deps)), []

def resolve_py_import(current_file, mod, level, project_root, names=None):
    if level is None:
        level=0
    if level==0:
        if not mod:
            return None
        base=mod.replace('.','/')
        candidates=[base+".py", os.path.join(base,"__init__.py")]
        for cand in candidates:
            rel=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
            if rel.startswith("./"):
                rel=rel[2:]
            if os.path.isfile(cand) or os.path.isfile(os.path.join(project_root, cand)):
                return rel
            alt=os.path.join(os.path.dirname(current_file), cand)
            altr=os.path.normpath(alt).replace(os.sep,"/")
            if altr.startswith("./"):
                altr=altr[2:]
            if os.path.isfile(alt):
                return altr
        return None
    else:
        base_dir=os.path.dirname(current_file)
        for _ in range(level-1):
            base_dir=os.path.dirname(base_dir)
        if mod:
            base=mod.replace('.','/')
            candidates=[os.path.join(base_dir, base+".py"), os.path.join(base_dir, base, "__init__.py")]
            for cand in candidates:
                if os.path.isfile(cand):
                    rel=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
                    if rel.startswith("./"):
                        rel=rel[2:]
                    return rel
            return None
        else:
            results=[]
            if names:
                for alias in names:
                    mod_name=alias.name
                    candidates=[os.path.join(base_dir, mod_name+".py"), os.path.join(base_dir, mod_name, "__init__.py")]

def parse_go_file(filepath):
    try:
        content=open(filepath,'r',errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    deps=[]
    errors=[]
    # find go.mod
    mod_name=None
    go_root=None
    cur=os.path.abspath(os.getcwd())
    while True:
        gm=os.path.join(cur, "go.mod")
        if os.path.isfile(gm):
            try:
                for line in open(gm).read().splitlines():
                    line=line.strip()
                    if line.startswith("module "):
                        mod_name=line.split()[1]
                        go_root=cur
                        break
            except:
                pass
            break
        parent=os.path.dirname(cur)
        if parent==cur:
            break
        cur=parent
    if not mod_name:
        return [], []
    imports=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'import\s*\(\s*([^)]*?)\s*\)', content, re.DOTALL):
        block=m.group(1)
        for q in re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', block):
            imports.append(q)
    for m in re.finditer(r'import\s+"([^"]+)"', content):
        imports.append(m.group(1))
    # dedupe
    imports=list(set(imports))
    for imp in imports:
        if mod_name and imp.startswith(mod_name):
            suffix=imp[len(mod_name):].lstrip("/")
            target_dir=os.path.join(go_root, suffix) if suffix else go_root
            if os.path.isdir(target_dir):
                for fname in os.listdir(target_dir):
                    if fname.endswith(".go"):
                        abs_file=os.path.join(target_dir, fname)
                        try:
                            rel=os.path.relpath(abs_file, os.getcwd()).replace(os.sep,"/")
                        except:
                            rel=os.path.join(suffix, fname).replace(os.sep,"/")
                        deps.append(rel)
            else:
                if os.path.isfile(target_dir+".go"):
                    rel=os.path.relpath(target_dir+".go", os.getcwd()).replace(os.sep,"/")
                    deps.append(rel)
                else:
                    errors.append(f"open {target_dir}: no such file or directory")
    return sorted(set(deps)), errors

def parse_rust_file(filepath):
    try:
        content=open(filepath,'r',errors='ignore').read()
    except:
        return [], []
    deps=[]
    errors=[]
    for m in re.finditer(r'^\s*(?:pub\s+)?mod\s+(\w+)\s*;', content, re.MULTILINE):
        mod=m.group(1)
        base_dir=os.path.dirname(filepath)
        candidates=[os.path.join(base_dir, mod+".rs"), os.path.join(base_dir, mod, "mod.rs"), os.path.join("src", mod+".rs"), os.path.join("src", mod, "mod.rs")]
        found=None
        for cand in candidates:
            if os.path.isfile(cand):
                found=os.path.normpath(cand).replace(os.sep,"/")
                if found.startswith("./"):
                    found=found[2:]
                break
        if found:
            deps.append(found)
        else:
            abs_dir=os.path.abspath(base_dir) if base_dir else os.path.abspath(".")
            errors.append(f"could not find mod {mod} while looking in dir {abs_dir}")
    return deps, errors

def parse_file(filepath, exclude_conditional=False):
    ext=os.path.splitext(filepath)[1]
    if ext==".py":
        return parse_python_file(filepath, exclude_conditional)
    elif ext in (".js",".ts",".jsx",".tsx",".mjs",".cjs"):
        return parse_js_file(filepath)
    elif ext==".go":
        return parse_go_file(filepath)
    elif ext==".rs":
        return parse_rust_file(filepath)
    else:
        return [], []

def build_graph(entry_files, exclude_patterns, only_patterns, python_exclude=False):
    graph={}
    errors={}
    visited=set()
    queue=entry_files[:]
    idx=0
    while idx < len(queue):
        f=queue[idx]
        idx+=1
        if f in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(f)
        if not os.path.isfile(f):
            continue
        deps, errs = parse_file(f, python_exclude)
        filtered=[]
        for d in deps:
            if not should_include(d, exclude_patterns, only_patterns):
                continue
            filtered.append(d)
            if d not in visited and d not in queue:
                queue.append(d)
        filtered=sorted(set(filtered))
        graph[f]=filtered
        if errs:
            errors[f]=errs
    return graph, errors, visited

def build_tree_structure(entry, graph):
    tree={}
    circular=[]
    def dfs(node, path):
        if node in path:
            idx=path.index(node)
            cycle=path[idx:]+[node]
            if cycle not in circular:
                circular.append(cycle)
            return None
        path.append(node)
        deps=graph.get(node, [])
        if not deps:
            path.pop()
            return None
        subtree={}
        for dep in deps:
            if dep in path:
                idx=path.index(dep)
                cycle=path[idx:]+[dep]
                if cycle not in circular:
                    circular.append(cycle)
                subtree[dep]=None
            else:
                child=dfs(dep, path)
                subtree[dep]=child
        path.pop()
        return subtree if subtree else None
    result=dfs(entry, [])
    if result is None:
        tree={entry: None}
    else:
        tree={entry: result}
    return tree, circular

def detect_all_cycles(graph):
    cycles=[]
    visited=set()
    stack=[]
    on_stack=set()
    def dfs(v):
        visited.add(v)
        stack.append(v)
        on_stack.add(v)
        for w in graph.get(v, []):
            if w not in visited:
                dfs(w)
            elif w in on_stack:
                idx=stack.index(w)
                cycle=stack[idx:]+[w]
                if cycle not in cycles:
                    cycles.append(cycle)
        stack.pop()
        on_stack.remove(v)
    for node in list(graph.keys()):
        if node not in visited:
            dfs(node)
    return cycles
